text:
olivia-cs: FYI Acme opened a P1 — their downstream JSON parser started failing after today's canary.
customer_acme: throwing the error: "Unexpected token i in JSON at position 1" when trying to parse the response from Redwood.
olivia-cs: they attached the raw response from our API, see below.
customer_acme: ```json
{ id: 123, details: { summary: "Line1\nLine2", tags: ["a","b",], }, }
```
customer_acme: note: that used to be valid JSON (keys quoted, no trailing commas). parser is strict (JSON.parse).
raj-eng: hmm — that looks like JS-style object literal: unquoted keys and trailing commas. We should never emit that. Which model/variant did you hit?
customer_acme: hitting model=redwood-2026-small-canary, content-type application/json, endpoint /v1/generate. We send structured-output schema in system prompt and max_tokens 400.
deploy-bot: canary rollout logged: model redwood-2026-small-canary deployed to canary pool at 2026-03-17T09:12:00Z by kevin-ml (job id c-8421).
kevin-ml: I pushed a prompt tuning update this morning to tighten "structured output" examples — didn't expect JS-literal output. Reproducing now.
kevin-ml: @raj-eng can you try a quick curl with the same prompt they used? if we can repro we should pin and rollback.
raj-eng: sharing the curl used by Acme (redacted api_key):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2026-small-canary","prompt":"Produce a JSON object matching this schema:\n{\"id\":number, \"details\":{\"summary\":string, \"tags\": [string]}}\nEnsure only valid JSON and no extra commentary."}'
```
raj-eng: response I got (raw):
```json
{ id: 999, details: { summary: "Hello\nWorld", tags: ["x","y",], }, }
```
raj-eng: repro confirmed. This is not valid JSON.
kevin-ml: OK that's on my change. Looks like the model started preferring compact JS-literal style in a few examples. Could be a formatting artifact introduced in the prompt examples.
olivia-cs: customer is blocked — their ingestion pipeline refuses the payload. They asked for an ETA/rollback.
raj-eng: suggested mitigations: 1) quick rollback of the prompt tuning on canary, 2) add stricter instruction to force double-quoted keys and no trailing commas, 3) temporary post-processing: if response fails JSON.parse, try to run a sanitizer to quote keys and remove trailing commas (hacky).
kevin-ml: rolling back the prompt patch from canary now (initiating), will monitor logs. If rollback doesn't resolve, I'll push a hard guard in the prompt: "Output must be valid JSON and parsable by JSON.parse; keys must use double quotes; no trailing commas." and add a final JSON validation check in the server response pipeline.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: canary model config reset at 2026-03-17T09:22:40Z (action id r-5512).
customer_acme: thanks — can you confirm when it's back to the old behavior? We'll keep their parser in fail-fast mode until confirmed.
kevin-ml: once rollback completes I'll test with the same curl and post raw output here. If it parses cleanly we'll ask you to retry.
raj-eng: noted for postmortem: add automated structured-output lint that runs JSON.parse on every generation for structured-output routes and flags regressions to alerts.
olivia-cs: +1 on alert. Also CS asked for a compensation credit if this impacts SLA — raising with account team.
customer_acme: appreciate the quick response :pray:\nPlease cc our SRE contact if you need more logs.
kevin-ml: rollback completed, testing now...\n(holding for final verification)
